features: The next deadline counted in days in the first screen, worked out from the visitor's own date
Seven services as a ledger: what you hand over, and what you get back
Three questions that light up the one line to start with
A sample year-end statement that settles from last year's figures to this year's, then ticks itself filed
A fee request that asks for a turnover band instead of publishing a price
name: Hale & Partners
short: An accountant's site that counts down to your next deadline from the first screen.
long: A practice site in ledger navy and white with one green for anything on time. The first screen shows a real office and the next tax deadline counted in days from the day you open the page, with the two after it underneath. Seven services sit as a ledger of what you hand over and what you get back, three questions light up the one to start with, and a sample year end settles from last year's figures to this year's before ticking itself filed.
proves: The dates and the figures do the selling. Nothing else has to.
story: Built to prove a quiet site can still work: no photographs of handshakes, no stock office, just the two things an accountant is actually judged on: the dates and the numbers.
